```{r setup5}
# Beta diversity parameters
source("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fconstancias/KU_Caroline/refs/heads/main/code/functions/phyloseq_functions.R")

# compute_plot_beta() 
# details:

#' @title This function calculates beta diversity, generates ordination plots (e.g., PCoA),  performs PERMANOVA, and optionally creates boxplots of distances between metadata groups.
#' @author Florentin Constancias
#' @param ps_up A phyloseq object containing microbiome data.
#' @param beta A list of distance matrices for beta diversity (e.g., Bray-Curtis, Aitchison).
#' @param m Character string specifying the ordination method (default: "PCoA").
#' @param color_group Character string for the variable used to color points in ordination plots (default: "Time").
#' @param shape_group Character string for the variable used to shape points in ordination plots (default: "Sample").
#' @param alpha Optional variable for transparency adjustment in ordination plots (default: NULL).
#' @param col_pal Color palette for point colors (default: `time_pal`).
#' @param fill_pal Fill color palette for point fills (default: `time_pal`).
#' @param path_group Character string for the variable grouping paths in ordination plots (default: "interaction(Sample,Subject)").
#' @param facet_formula Formula for faceting ordination plots (default: "Sample ~ .").
#' @param axis1 Integer specifying the ordination axis to plot on the x-axis (default: 1).
#' @param axis2 Integer specifying the ordination axis to plot on the y-axis (default: 2).
#' @param seed Integer for random seed, ensuring reproducible results in ordination (default: 123).
#' @param permanova_terms Character vector of variables for PERMANOVA tests (default: c("Time", "cluster_Dtp2")).
#' @param metadata_dist_boxplot Optional variable for generating distance boxplots (default: NULL).
#' @param strata Variable for stratified PERMANOVA testing (default: "none").
#' @param perm Number of permutations for PERMANOVA (default: 999).
#' 
#' @return A list of results, including:
#'   - `pcoas`: Ordination plots with faceting and custom color/shape groups.
#'   - `expl_var`: Explained variance for each axis in ordination plots.
#'   - `PCOA`: Detailed ordination plot for the rAitchison distance with paths.
#'   - `PCOA_leg`: Legend for the ordination plot.
#'   - `perm`: PERMANOVA results.
#'   - `pw_perm`: Pairwise PERMANOVA results for each variable in `permanova_terms`.
#'   - `tw_perm`: Two-way PERMANOVA results for each variable in `permanova_terms`.
#'   - Optional: `dist_boxplot` if `metadata_dist_boxplot` is provided, showing boxplots of distances.
```

# Calculate MetaPhlAn beta diversity distances
```{r MetaPhlAn data transformation}
# MetaPhlAn data transformation for beta diversity analysis
# Calculates bjaccard, wjaccard and rAitchison beta diversity measures
beta <- ps_up %>%
  subset_taxa(Class != "UNCLASSIFIED") %>% 
  transform_sample_counts(function(x) x/sum(x) * 1) %>% 
  phyloseq_compute_bdiv()
```

## MetaPhlAn, saliva, baseline
```{r distances taxa SALIVA BASELINE, warning=FALSE}
# Subset phyloseq object
ps_tmp <- ps_up %>%
        subset_samples(Sample == "Saliva" & Period == "Baseline") %>%
        subset_taxa(Class != "UNCLASSIFIED") %>% 
        transform_sample_counts(function(x) x/sum(x) * 1)

# Extract OTU table
otu_mat <- as(otu_table(ps_tmp), "matrix") %>% t()
# Assign sample names explicitly
rownames(otu_mat) <- sample_names(ps_tmp)

# Robust CLR transformation
clr_mat <- vegan::decostand(otu_mat, "rclr") 
# Assign sample names explicitly
rownames(clr_mat) <- sample_names(ps_tmp)

# Assign Robust Aitchison distance to beta variable
beta$rAitchison <- vegan::vegdist(clr_mat, method = "euclidean") %>% 
  magrittr::divide_by(100)

# Remove Bray-Curtis and Sørensen beta
beta$bray <- NULL 
beta$sorensen <- NULL 

hopkins(clr_mat, n = nrow(clr_mat)-1)

# Interpretation of the Hopkins statistic is:
# 
# ~0.5 → random structure / no meaningful clusters
# close to 0 → highly uniform/regular spacing
# close to 1 → strong cluster tendency
```

## Optimal number of clusters
```{r optimal clusters}
# Elbow method on CLR data
set.seed(123)

wss <- numeric(10)

for (k in 1:10) {
  km <- kmeans(clr_mat, centers = k, nstart = 25)
  wss[k] <- km$tot.withinss
}

plot(1:10, wss, type = "b", pch = 19,
     xlab = "Number of clusters (k)",
     ylab = "Total within-cluster sum of squares")

# Silhouette method on Robust Aithison distances
sil_width <- numeric(10)

for (k in 2:10) {
  groups <- cutree(hclust(beta$rAitchison, method = "average"), k = k)
  sil <- silhouette(groups, beta$rAitchison)
  sil_width[k] <- mean(sil[, 3])
}

plot(2:10, sil_width[2:10], type = "b", pch = 19,
     xlab = "Number of clusters (k)",
     ylab = "Average silhouette width")
```
For these samples, the optimal number of clusters are 3. 

## Cut groups into optimal number of clusters
```{r}
# Perform hierarchical clustering
clust <- hclust(beta$rAitchison, method = "average")

# Plot dendrogram
#plot(clust)

# Cut dendrogram into optimal number of clusters
groups <- cutree(clust, k = 3)

groups
```

```{r add cluster to temporary phyloseq object}
sample_data(ps_tmp)$Cluster <- factor(groups[sample_names(ps_tmp)])
```

```{r visualize taxa, warning=FALSE}
ord <- ordinate(ps_tmp, method = "PCoA", distance = beta$rAitchison)

p_clust_tax_saliva_baseline <- plot_ordination(ps_tmp, ord, color = "Cluster", shape = "Inflammation_response") +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = cluster_colors) +
  labs(shape = "Responder groups", color = "Microbiota cluster") +
  theme_light() + theme_linedraw() +    
  theme(legend.position = "none")

p_clust_tax_saliva_baseline
```
```{r}
p_clust_tax_saliva_baseline <- p_clust_tax_saliva_baseline + labs(title = "", x = "Axis 1 [52%]", y = "Axis 2 [44.2%]")

p_clust_tax_saliva_baseline
```

```{r bar plot}
# Convert sample_data to a data frame
metadata <- data.frame(sample_data(ps_tmp))

# Make sure variables are factors
metadata$Cluster <- factor(metadata$Cluster)
metadata$Inflammation_response <- factor(metadata$Inflammation_response)

# Summarise counts and proportions
df_plot <- metadata %>%
  group_by(Cluster, Inflammation_response) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Cluster) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n))

p_bar_tax_saliva_baseline <- ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = Cluster, y = prop, fill = Inflammation_response)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "fill", color = "black", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = n),
    position = position_fill(vjust = 0.5),
    size = 4
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = infl_pal) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  labs(
    title = "", 
    x = "Microbiota cluster",
    y = "Proportion of participants",
    fill = "Responder group"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

p_bar_tax_saliva_baseline
```

```{r statistic}
# Create contingency table
tab <- table(metadata$Cluster, metadata$Inflammation_response)

# Pearson's Chi-square test
fisher.test(tab)

# Effect size (Cramér's V)
library(rcompanion)
cramerV(tab)
```

## MetaPhlAn, plaque, week 2
```{r distances taxa PLAQUE WEEK 2, warning=FALSE}
# Subset phyloseq object
ps_tmp <- ps_up %>%
        subset_samples(Sample == "Plaque" & Period == "Week 2") %>%
        subset_taxa(Class != "UNCLASSIFIED") %>% 
        transform_sample_counts(function(x) x/sum(x) * 1)

# Extract OTU table
otu_mat <- as(otu_table(ps_tmp), "matrix") %>% t()
# Assign sample names explicitly
rownames(otu_mat) <- sample_names(ps_tmp)

# Robust CLR transformation
clr_mat <- vegan::decostand(otu_mat, "rclr") 
# Assign sample names explicitly
rownames(clr_mat) <- sample_names(ps_tmp)

# Assign Robust Aitchison distance to beta variable
beta$rAitchison <- vegan::vegdist(clr_mat, method = "euclidean") %>% 
  magrittr::divide_by(100)

# Remove Bray-Curtis and Sørensen beta
beta$bray <- NULL 
beta$sorensen <- NULL 

hopkins(clr_mat, n = nrow(clr_mat)-1)
```

## Optimal number of clusters
```{r optimal clusters}
# Elbow method on CLR data
set.seed(123)

wss <- numeric(10)

for (k in 1:10) {
  km <- kmeans(clr_mat, centers = k, nstart = 25)
  wss[k] <- km$tot.withinss
}

plot(1:10, wss, type = "b", pch = 19,
     xlab = "Number of clusters (k)",
     ylab = "Total within-cluster sum of squares")

# Silhouette method on Robust Aithison distances
sil_width <- numeric(10)

for (k in 2:10) {
  groups <- cutree(hclust(beta$rAitchison, method = "average"), k = k)
  sil <- silhouette(groups, beta$rAitchison)
  sil_width[k] <- mean(sil[, 3])
}

plot(2:10, sil_width[2:10], type = "b", pch = 19,
     xlab = "Number of clusters (k)",
     ylab = "Average silhouette width")
```
For these samples, the optimal number of clusters is 2. 

## Cut groups into optimal number of clusters
```{r}
# Perform hierarchical clustering 
clust <- hclust(beta$rAitchison, method = "average") 

# Plot dendrogram 
#plot(clust)

# Cut dendrogram into optimal number of clusters
groups <- cutree(clust, k = 2) 

groups
```

```{r add cluster to temporary phyloseq object}
sample_data(ps_tmp)$Cluster <- factor(groups[sample_names(ps_tmp)])
```

```{r visualize taxa, warning=FALSE}
ord <- ordinate(ps_tmp, method = "PCoA", distance = beta$rAitchison)

p_clust_tax_plaque_week2 <- plot_ordination(ps_tmp, ord, color = "Cluster", shape = "Inflammation_response") +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = cluster_colors) +
  labs(shape = "Responder groups", color = "Microbiota cluster") +
  theme_light() + theme_linedraw() +    
  theme(legend.position = "none")

p_clust_tax_plaque_week2
```

```{r}
p_clust_tax_plaque_week2 <- p_clust_tax_plaque_week2 +  labs(title = "", 
                                                                   x = "Axis 1 [57.5%]", y = "Axis 2 [32.6%]")

p_clust_tax_plaque_week2
```

```{r bar plot}
# Convert sample_data to a data frame
metadata <- data.frame(sample_data(ps_tmp))

# Make sure variables are factors
metadata$Cluster <- factor(metadata$Cluster)
metadata$Inflammation_response <- factor(metadata$Inflammation_response)

# Summarise counts and proportions
df_plot <- metadata %>%
  group_by(Cluster, Inflammation_response) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Cluster) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n))

p_bar_tax_plaque_week2 <- ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = Cluster, y = prop, fill = Inflammation_response)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "fill", color = "black", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = n),
    position = position_fill(vjust = 0.5),
    size = 4
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = infl_pal) +

  labs(
    title = "", 
    x = "Microbiota cluster",
    y = "Proportion of participants",
    fill = "Responder group"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

p_bar_tax_plaque_week2

  phyloseq_compute_bdiv()

  magrittr::divide_by(100)

# Remove Bray-Curtis and Sørensen
beta_pway$bray <- NULL
beta_pway$sorensen <- NULL

hopkins(clr_mat, n = nrow(clr_mat)-1)
```

## Optimal number of clusters
```{r optimal clusters}
# Elbow method on CLR data
set.seed(123)

wss <- numeric(10)

for (k in 1:10) {
  km <- kmeans(clr_mat, centers = k, nstart = 25)
  wss[k] <- km$tot.withinss
}

plot(1:10, wss, type = "b", pch = 19,
     xlab = "Number of clusters (k)",
     ylab = "Total within-cluster sum of squares")

# Silhouette method on Robust Aithison distances
sil_width <- numeric(10)

for (k in 2:10) {
  groups <- cutree(hclust(beta_pway$rAitchison, method = "average"), k = k)
  sil <- silhouette(groups, beta_pway$rAitchison)
  sil_width[k] <- mean(sil[, 3])
}

plot(2:10, sil_width[2:10], type = "b", pch = 19,
     xlab = "Number of clusters (k)",
     ylab = "Average silhouette width")
```
For these samples, the optimal number of clusters is 3. 

## Cut groups into optimal number of clusters
```{r}
# Perform hierarchical clustering 
clust <- hclust(beta_pway$rAitchison, method = "average") 

# Plot dendrogram 
#plot(clust)

# Cut dendrogram into optimal number of clusters
groups <- cutree(clust, k = 3) 

groups
```

```{r add cluster to temporary phyloseq object}
sample_data(ps_tmp)$Cluster <- factor(groups[sample_names(ps_tmp)])
```

```{r visualize taxa, warning=FALSE}
ord <- ordinate(ps_tmp, method = "PCoA", distance = beta_pway$rAitchison)

p_clust_pway_plaque_baseline <- plot_ordination(ps_tmp, ord, color = "Cluster", shape = "Inflammation_response") +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = cluster_colors) +
  labs(shape = "Responder groups", color = "Microbiota cluster") +
  theme_light() + theme_linedraw() +    
  theme(legend.position = "none") 

p_clust_pway_plaque_baseline
```

```{r}
p_clust_pway_plaque_baseline <- p_clust_pway_plaque_baseline +  labs(title = "", 
                                                                   x = "Axis 1 [52.9%]", y = "Axis 2 [42.2%]")

p_clust_pway_plaque_baseline
```

```{r bar plot}
# Convert sample_data to a data frame
metadata <- data.frame(sample_data(ps_tmp))

# Make sure variables are factors
metadata$Cluster <- factor(metadata$Cluster)
metadata$Inflammation_response <- factor(metadata$Inflammation_response)

# Summarise counts and proportions
df_plot <- metadata %>%
  group_by(Cluster, Inflammation_response) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Cluster) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n))

p_bar_pway_plaque_baseline <- ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = Cluster, y = prop, fill = Inflammation_response)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "fill", color = "black", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = n),
    position = position_fill(vjust = 0.5),
    size = 4
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = infl_pal) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  labs(
    title = "", 
    x = "Microbiota cluster",
    y = "Proportion of participants",
    fill = "Responder group"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

p_bar_pway_plaque_baseline
```

```{r statistic}
# Create contingency table
tab <- table(metadata$Cluster, metadata$Inflammation_response)

# Pearson's Chi-square test
fisher.test(tab)

# Effect size (Cramér's V)
cramerV(tab)
```
